item.title: [42wim/matterircd] matterircd v0.35.0
item.description:
42wim/matterircd | 309 stars| 63 forks.

| Go | Dockerfile | Makefile |

Connect to your mattermost or slack using your IRC-client of choice.

New features

  • general: Add support for additional AI providers for EXPERIMENTAL AI summarizing of posts/threads/channels
    • OpenAI & OpenAI-compatible providers (#952)
    • DeepSeek (#1010)
    • Claude (#1011)
    • xAI & Meta Muse (#1012)
    • Google AI Studio API keys for Gemini (#1023)
    • OpenRouter (#1089)
  • matrix: Add EXPERIMENTAL support for [matrix] bridge (#912, #951)
    • Support edits, deletions, typing, topics, membership, files, history, search, reactions, status, and spaces (#951)
    • Support end-to-end encryption (E2EE) via goolm build tag, device ID/session key display, verification status on login, interactive SAS device verification, and in-chat verification of other users (#951, #960, #966, #967, #969, #978)
    • Support room invitations and accepting them with /join (#965)
    • Support shared Mattermost config options, service commands, DefaultProvider, and configurable nick format (matrix.ReplaceColonChar) (#955, #958, #990)
    • Support WHOIS details, user status, and DirectoryURL (restricted to DefaultProvider homeserver) (#977, #1046, #1064)
    • Support emoji/unicode suffixes, deleted message text, pinned/unpinned events, and reaction removals with thread context (#991, #1020, #1043)
  • slack: Overhaul Slack bridge using matterbridge/slackclient to achieve feature and config parity with Mattermost and Matrix (#1030, #1049, #1057, #1058, #1060)
    • Add xoxc/xoxd cookie login support and RTM WebSocket authentication (#1030)
    • Add thread IDs, message actions, DETAILS URLs, reactions, typing, file events/attachments, nick, ping, and member counts (#1039, #1048, #1056)
    • Add service commands (SUMMARIZE, SEARCH, SCROLLBACK, DETAILS, etc.) and scrollback/replay history support (#1045)
    • Add real-time lifecycle sync events, disconnect/reconnect notices, WHOIS details, custom status & expiration, and workspace-scoped DirectoryURL support (#1046, #1047, #1051, #1055, #1065)
    • Add Block Kit rendering, unfurl previews, quoted code blocks, archive link IDs, and Mattermost-style pinned/unpinned & attachment formatting (#1043, #1044, #1049, #1058, #1060)
    • Support Slack RealName and Enterprise Grid nick resolution (#1037)

Enhancement

  • general: Refactor AI summarization into a dedicated ai package with updated default models, retry/backoff on timeouts and transient errors, and streaming JSON decoding (#1024, #1026, #1027, #1032)
  • general: Include AI provider, model, thinking mode, and detailed token usage (input cache hit/miss and output tokens) in summary notices & footer, and log summarization requests and metrics at INFO level (#1022, #1025, #1085, #1088)
  • general: Support model overrides in SUMMARIZE and resolve shorthand Gemini model names (#1086)
  • general: Support per-protocol lastviewed databases and namespace global event timestamps (#1003)
  • general: Route IRC PASS to the bridge matching its Restrict list (#983)
  • general: Consolidate SharedConfig fields across bridges and improve live config reload (#1061, #1062)
  • general: Expand credential redaction in logs (#1050)
  • general: Prioritize primary emoji aliases over tags and support inline closing code fences with bridge suffixes (#1041, #1042)
  • general: Trigger Docker workflow on v* tag pushes to publish versioned images (#1091)
  • irc: Make IRC max line length configurable (MaxLineLength) (#1082)
  • irc: Support !! in @@ reaction syntax to react to the last sent message (#1017)
  • irc: Use WHOIS identity in channel message prefixes and honor wire limits (#970)
  • irc: Route login and sync progress to SERVER NOTICEs for PASS logins (#1019)
  • irc: Route channel delivery failures as ERR_CANNOTSENDTOCHAN (404) (#1018)
  • irc: Send replay headers as IRC NOTICE (#1090, #1093)
  • irc: Only expose the service bot of the connected bridge (#1087)
  • irc: Wait for login OK before starting channel sync and history replay (#1052)
  • irc: Attach IRCv3 @time= server-time tags to delayed live events (#1063)
  • matrix: Update matrixclient and filter unused Matrix events in /sync with a denylist (#975, #996, #998, #1000, #1002, #1014, #1016, #1070)
  • matrix: Honour MatrixclientLogLevel, include room names in log messages, and log API calls and round-trip durations (#960, #976, #992, #1005)
  • matrix: Reduce memory allocations and optimize member lookups, user resolution, and room queries (#1013, #1029)
  • matrix: Process synced events on a worker goroutine and isolate initial sync (#997, #1005)
  • matrix: Show own edits, deletions, and reactions with thread context, and track parent thread IDs in /lastsent (#1006, #1015)
  • matrix: Support HideReactions and DisableShowOwnModified config options (#1049)
  • matrix: Trigger channel sync after long disconnects (#1040)
  • mattermost: Support Mattermost 12 and warn instead of failing on Mattermost versions below 7 (#1076, #1078)
  • mattermost: Log Mattermost API round-trip durations (#1005)
  • mattermost: Speed up Mattermost logout (#959)
  • mattermost: Refresh offline/away status sooner and use GetStatusFresh for RPL_AWAY/WHOIS last-online info (#971, #972)
  • slack: Cache channel metadata, joined state, and channel members (#1053)
  • slack: Reduce lock contention, allocations, and logout blocking (#1072)
  • slack: Align Slack API logging with Mattermost and Matrix and stop echoing tokens to IRC (#1030)

Bugfix

  • general: Self-heal channel and room names for Mattermost and Matrix (#962)
  • general: Do not fall back to regular message on network errors when replying to a thread (#999)
  • general: Check HTTP status code before decoding Copilot AI response (#1009)
  • general: Make Mattermost and Matrix post retries idempotent to prevent duplicate messages on timeouts (#1031)
  • general: Use wall-clock time for heavy sync threshold check (#1059)
  • general: Snapshot BoltDB last-viewed cursors before replay sync, defer cursor updates for channels pending replay, and skip cursor updates when IRC socket writes fail (#1075, #1077, #1081)
  • general: Restore 1000-event buffer on bridge eventChan (#1080)
  • irc: Fall back to channel typing when thread root can't be resolved (#974)
  • irc: Fix outbound DM sender nick and isolate Mattermost webhook override_username ghosts (#1028)
  • matrix: Fix splitting / wrapping of lines & add HardLineSplit to prevent IRC message/line truncation (#953)
  • matrix: Fix auto-join, incoming messages, DMs, echoes, identities, and logging (#954)
  • matrix: Accept saved channel names carrying the default provider on join and keep channel name of restored rooms (#957, #1001)
  • matrix: Show inferred DMs, handle channel <-> DM transitions, skip unjoined m.direct rooms, classify new DM rooms before persisting, and hide in-flight DM rooms (#968, #981, #982, #984)
  • matrix: Force a full initial sync on start when E2EE is enabled (#973)
  • matrix: Fix ghost nicks in typing/replay/search to use localpart/homeserver nicks (#989)
  • matrix: Skip deleted notices for redacted edits (#993)
  • matrix: Don't send typing indicators for threads (#995)
  • matrix: Resolve thread root when replying within a thread and resolve room fallback in GetPostThread (#1007, #1008)
  • matrix: Fix topic updates for local non-public rooms and DMs (#1021)
  • matrix: Avoid duplicating /sync-delivered messages on reconnect (#1063, #1083)
  • matrix: Fix empty parent reply context in E2EE rooms (#1071)
  • matrix: Preserve event ordering for room updates, initial invites, and E2EE late keys (#1073)
  • mattermost: Refresh Mattermost HTTP session on 401 Unauthorized (#1033)
  • mattermost: Stabilize postListToEvents sort and guard nil posts (#1079)
  • slack: Route Slackbot system messages to system and use IRC nick for Adder/Remover (#1035)
  • slack: Handle Slack channel_topic and channel_purpose events, and fix channel renames and private topic/purpose metadata (#1036, #1054)
  • slack: Validate Slack token format on PASS auto-login (#1038)
  • slack: Fix startup ordering, replay boundary duplicate, live update @time, and echo suppression (#1074)

item.title: [meta/flow] v0.342.0
item.description:
meta/flow | 22318 stars| 1892 forks.

| Shell | JavaScript | Makefile | Ruby | CSS | Vim Snippet | TypeScript | Rust | RenderScript | MDX |

Adds static typing to JavaScript to improve developer productivity and code quality.

Likely to cause new Flow errors:

  • A failed attempt to match a member of a union no longer changes the types that later attempts see, which can find errors that were missed. (e.g. try-Flow)
  • Flow now infers the type arguments of a generic call by matching its arguments and its expected type against the signature directly, rather than by solving temporary type variables through subtyping. Some inferred types change, and some errors move from an argument to the place where the call's result is used.
  • Errors about a type application (a type that is not polymorphic, a value used as a type) are now reported once, where the application is written, including for applications of generic type parameters and of any-typed values
  • untyped-type-import errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • internal-type errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • invalid-this-arg errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • libdef-override errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • nested-component errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already, but all=warn, all=off or an explicit setting could weaken it). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • nested-hook errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already, but all=warn, all=off or an explicit setting could weaken it). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • unsafe-object-assign errors are now always on (the lint was on by default already, but all=warn, all=off or an explicit setting could weaken it). Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • react-intrinsic-overlap errors are now always on and can no longer be turned off with lint settings. Suppress them with $FlowFixMe[react-intrinsic-overlap]. Delete references to the lint in your .flowconfig and flowlint comments — the setting is a no-op for this release and will be removed in a future release.
  • T[K] of an optional property now includes void; some errors involving optional properties are reported at different locations or with different codes.

New Features:

  • undefined is always accepted as a type annotation. experimental.undefined_type only accepts true.

Notable bug fixes:

  • An interface that extends a type alias whose type parameters all have defaults no longer loses the members it inherits when imported
  • Type references inside a declare namespace block now resolve classes, enums and values declared in the namespace's other blocks, as they already did when the declaration was imported
  • A callback parameter's hint no longer includes void from members of a union hint that do not take the parameter.
  • Arguments of yield, yield* and return in annotated generators are now checked with the annotation as a hint, as in TypeScript, and AsyncGenerator is covariant in its yield and return types like Generator.
  • Testing a property against a union of literals that includes null or undefined no longer drops members whose property is null or void. Under experimental.ts_void, testing a property against undefined or a literal narrows away members whose property is void.
  • Under experimental.ts_void, fixed a spurious missing-local-annot on a callback whose call has another callback that returns no value.
  • Type-argument errors on new of a value with a construct signature are reported at the new expression instead of the signature's declaration.
  • Promise.resolve() returns Promise<void>, and a return hint no longer makes an overloaded call fail when an overload accepts its arguments.

Misc:

  • Document the flow-upgrade package on flow.org.

item.description:

Open-source search database for full-text, vector, and hybrid search with real-time indexing and SQL.

Version 32.1.3

Released: November 20th 2026

This release adds direct-to-disk bulk import for real-time, sharded, and replicated tables, including concurrent shared loads; improves KNN, hybrid, and full-text search performance; expands auto-embedding and diagnostics capabilities; and fixes issues with replication, query correctness, data integrity, packaging, and shutdown. See the cluster upgrade notes below before upgrading from an older version.

❤️ We'd like to thank @tudorvasinca for PR #4858, PR #4924, and PR #4925; @vitlav for PR #5060; @RaphaelFakhri for PR #5031; and @drahy333 for Columnar PR #217.

Upgrading from 29.9.0

Not using replication? Skip these steps. No special migration is needed for standalone instances.

The replication protocol has changed, so rolling upgrades are not supported:

  1. Check that all nodes are synchronized, stop writes, and back up your data.
  2. Stop all nodes one at a time, waiting for each to shut down cleanly. Remember which one stopped last.
  3. Upgrade all nodes to 32.1.3 while they are stopped. Prevent automatic restarts during the upgrade.
  4. Start the last stopped node first with manticore_new_cluster (systemd) or searchd --new-cluster, then start the others normally. Wait for all nodes to synchronize before resuming writes.

If the cluster shut down unexpectedly, use the cluster recovery guide instead.

Breaking Changes

  • ⚠️ v32.0.0 PR #5101 Added bulk import for replicated tables and changed how replicated table files are tracked. This is incompatible with older versions: upgrade every cluster node together, not one by one. See Upgrading from 29.9.0.
  • ⚠️ v31.0.0 Issue #5016 In real-time mode, Manticore stores its table and cluster list in manticore.json under data_dir (usually /var/lib/manticore/manticore.json). A power loss could previously leave it empty. Manticore now saves it more safely and refuses to start with an empty file rather than silently losing the table list. Most users need no action. If startup reports file is empty, restore a valid backup; do not delete the file.
  • ⚠️ v30.0.0 PR #5015 Cluster joins now check that all nodes can reach the joining node before transferring data. The replication change is incompatible with older versions; see Upgrading from 29.9.0.

New Features and Improvements

  • 🆕 v32.1.0 Commit Bulk import now passes the table's configured indexer and common options to the bulk indexer and builds chunks with the table's external files, making imported data consistent with the table configuration.
  • 🆕 v32.0.0 PR #5101 Extended direct-to-disk bulk import to sharded tables over HTTP and SQL, including replicated shards. The coordinator routes documents to their shards, runs indexers on shard nodes, and publishes each shard's disk chunk on commit; PURGE BULK_IMPORT can clean up unfinished shared loads. On replicated tables, chunks are transferred to replicas and attached through replication, with SST recovery for nodes that missed a file change.
  • 🆕 v31.0.24 PR #5013 Issue #5110 Improved full-text search with dictionary-based COUNT(*) for eligible single-term queries and rank-free counting for more complex queries. Added 4,096-row bitmap windows for eligible OR/AND counts and unranked queries, SIMD bitmap operations, faster postings readers, redundant-filter elimination, and GROUP BY blob prefetch. SHOW META identifies FastCount, RanklessCount, WindowOrCount, and WindowAndCount execution paths.
  • 🆕 v31.0.24 PR #5013 Issue #5110 Changed the default access_doclists and access_hitlists to mmap instead of buffered file reads and added a configurable skiplist_cache_size to reduce repeated skiplist decompression.
  • 🆕 v31.0.23 PR #5013 Issue #5110 Tagged an intermediate version of the full-text counting and postings optimizations on their development branch; the completed changes were integrated into main in v31.0.24.
  • 🆕 v31.0.20 PR #5092 Updated Executor to 1.4.8 with a newer LLM extension revision.
  • 🆕 v31.0.17 PR #5074 Updated Executor to 1.4.7, including an updated LLM dependency.
  • 🆕 v31.0.2 PR #5021 Updated Executor to 1.4.6 (including PHP 8.5.12 security fixes) and Buddy to 4.4.9, which avoids PHP 8.5 deprecation errors in fuzzy search and autocomplete when a character has no keyboard-layout mapping.
  • 🆕 v29.18.6 PR #4987 Made crash dumps identify the current operation and table, including background optimizations, RT flushes, merges, rotation, replication-related work, and SQL/HTTP requests, rather than sometimes reporting a previous query.
  • 🆕 v29.18.0 PR #4994 Extended knn_rescore_prefetch to row-wise vector storage, reading candidate row headers and full-precision vectors in parallel when data is not already cached.
  • 🆕 v29.17.0 PR #5005 Added automatic document-ID generation to bulk_import, so inputs need not supply every ID.
  • 🆕 v29.16.0 PR #5000 Added highlighting for auto-chunked embedding text: a KNN result can highlight the chunk that matched the query rather than only the original full text.
  • 🆕 v29.15.0 PR #4999 Introduced shared HTTP bulk import: concurrent /bulk?bulk_import=<table>&shared[=N] requests feed one table-wide indexer pool and publish up to N disk chunks on commit. Added session-aware cleanup through PURGE BULK_IMPORT and support for bare document lines.
  • 🆕 v29.15.0 PR #4996 Added indextool --docstore-bad-ids to list live document IDs affected by damaged stored-field blocks so they can be reinserted; indextool --check now detects missing or zero-filled docstore blocks.
  • 🆕 v29.14.6 manticore-load PR #29 Updated manticore-load with opt-in --realistic text generation for benchmarking: frequency-weighted English vocabulary, natural document-length variation, repeated terms, and <text/common/...>, <text/medium/...>, and <text/rare/...> query terms. The previous synthetic generator remains the default.
  • 🆕 v29.14.2 Issue #4929 Made HNSW graph construction during FLUSH RAMCHUNK parallel, splitting RAM chunks into balanced row ranges so knn_parallel_build can improve flush speed.
  • 🆕 v29.14.0 PR #4969 Optimized KNN search with a per-table rescoring budget, prefetch for columnar full-precision vectors, and adaptive HNSW early_termination on agents. knn_rescore_prefetch reduces cold-cache vector reads without changing matches.

item.description:
bblimke/webmock | 4047 stars| 590 forks.

| Ruby |

Library for stubbing and setting expectations on HTTP requests in Ruby.

  • Fix matching of indexed arrays nested inside arrays of hashes (#1144)

    Previously, WebMock read indexed arrays nested inside an array of hashes, such as a[][b][0][c]=1, as hashes with "0", "1" keys. WebMock writes that form itself, so with(query: {"a" => [{"b" => [{"c" => "1"}]}]}) with a regexp URI did not match ?a[][b][][c]=1, and a Typhoeus request with that hash as its body did not match a stub with the same hash.

    If a stub uses the old shape, such as {"a" => [{"b" => {"0" => {"c" => "1"}}}]}, for example one copied from WebMock's suggested stub, use arrays instead.

    Thanks to Hamza Tarar

  • Fix matching of arrays of hashes that repeat a nested key

    Previously, WebMock put a nested key repeated under [] into the first hash of the array, so items[][address][city]=X&items[][address][city]=Y was read as one item with the city Y. A stub listing both items did not match, and a stub for X and Y also matched a request for Z and Y. Rails and Faraday encode arrays of nested hashes this way.

    Such keys now go into a new hash, as in Rack. If a stub lists such an array as one item, for example one copied from WebMock's suggested stub, list every item.

    Queries that mix a value and nested keys under the same name, such as a[][b]=1&a[][b][c]=2 or a[c]=1&a[c][]=2, no longer raise IndexError or join the values into one string.

  • Apply Net::HTTP response_body_encoding to stubbed response bodies (#1138)

    Previously, stubbed Net::HTTP responses ignored Net::HTTP#response_body_encoding= and Net::HTTPResponse#body_encoding=. A body stubbed as binary, for example from a raw response file, stayed ASCII-8BIT even with http.response_body_encoding = true and a Content-Type of text/plain; charset=utf-8.

    Stubbed bodies now get the encoding real responses get: with true, the charset from the Content-Type header or an HTML <meta> tag, and otherwise the encoding the setting names. Without the setting, a body keeps the encoding it was stubbed with.

    Thanks to Yang Bai

  • Give each stubbed Net::HTTP response its own copy of the body

    Previously, a stubbed Net::HTTP response returned the stubbed body string itself. A body stubbed with a frozen string, such as a literal in a file with # frozen_string_literal: true, made response.body.force_encoding("UTF-8") raise FrozenError, which a real response never does. Changing the body in place, for example with response.body << "!", changed it for later requests to the same stub too.

  • Keep the size of async-http responses to HEAD requests (#1143)

    async-http gives the size of a response to a HEAD request as response.body.length, not as a header. Previously, a response stubbed with stub_request(:head, url).to_return(headers: {"Content-Length" => "42"}) ignored the Content-Length: its body was nil over HTTP/1 and had a length of 0 over HTTP/2. A real response lost its size, with a nil body, when a WebMock.after_request callback was registered, for example while VCR was recording, and the recorded response had no Content-Length.

    A stubbed response now takes its size from the stubbed Content-Length, or from the stubbed body without one, as before. A real response keeps its size when a callback is registered, and the recorded response has it as its Content-Length.

    Thanks to Andrew K. Fader

  • Keep the URI query of HTTPClient requests that pass a query argument (#1145)

    Previously, WebMock dropped the query in the URI when an HTTPClient request also passed the query argument. HTTPClient.new.get("http://example.com/?a=1", {"b" => "2"}) requests /?a=1&b=2, but WebMock saw /?b=2, and with {} as the query argument it saw no query at all. A stub or a_request expectation could match a URL that was never requested.

    If a stub or expectation for such a request leaves out the query in the URI, add it, for example stub_request(:get, "http://example.com/?a=1&b=2"). Record VCR cassettes with such requests again.

    Thanks to AmeenKhan12345

Highlights:

  • GNU Compatibility

    • sort rejects conflicting -t, --compress-program and --check modes, validates --parallel like GNU, and rejects --debug together with -c/-C; merge batches and temporary files are handled more carefully
    • date matches the GNU case flags on %c, %p, %P, %r and %Z, keeps leading zeros of %N with a width, and uses the locale date format verbatim
    • dd: conv=ibm, conv=block and conv=unblock behave like GNU, and excl/nofollow are checked before seeking in an output FIFO
    • ls accepts unambiguous --time-style prefixes, applies two-line time formats to old and recent files correctly, and sorts command-line arguments by version properly
    • tail follows a symlink to its target, accepts the obsolete -cf form, and clamps --max-unchanged-stats instead of overflowing
    • printf and seq fix %f padding past 1000 zeros; split accepts a leading + in every number and retries short writes; pr, numfmt, stty, stat and od align more options and messages with GNU

  • Safer File Handling

    • cp no longer writes a recursive copy through a symlinked target, and checks relative symlink destinations against the working directory
    • mv and ln refuse to replace a directory with a symlink (or with --backup, -f, -i in ln)
    • chown/chgrp judge --preserve-root on the stat the traversal is pinned to; chmod -R -L reports dangling symlinks
    • install backs up a dangling symlink destination; install, cp and mknod warn when an explicit security context is ignored
    • rm escapes the operand in the --preserve-root error message
    • uucore: fixed EOVERFLOW in safe traversal

  • Robustness

    • Panics fixed on write failures for verbose output in rmdir, chcon, cp and tail, on write errors in numfmt, and in printf/seq on zero
    • Non-UTF-8 input is now preserved in date (format strings and --reference), stat error messages and shred diagnostics
    • uucore parses a NaN payload such as nan(1) and quotes a lone brace in the shell quoting styles; c-maybe quoting is supported

  • Performance

    • tr deletes bytes faster, basenc encodes and decodes base58 faster, and od streams its output line by line instead of buffering it

  • Dependency Diet

    • chroot, sync and the permission helpers use std instead of rustix; cp and dd use set_len instead of ftruncate; uucore no longer needs unsafe for gettid

  • Cross-platform Reach

    • WASI: integration tests enabled for seq, mv, fmt, readlink, dircolors, cksum, realpath, nproc, shred and join, a macro to document why a test is ignored, date clock support, and nice is no longer part of the default WASI build
    • Windows: ln converts / to \ in symlink targets, and cp handles a recursive copy of a root such as W:/
    • uucore detects ASIMD on big-endian aarch64 and builds stty on little-endian ppc64

  • Upstream: while chasing compatibility we found behavior GNU's own suite did not cover, and contributed 82 commits to GNU coreutils during this cycle, almost all of them new tests for edge cases both implementations share, plus two small fixes (tail, fmt)

  • Contributions: This release landed 931 pull requests from 92 new contributors

item.title: [mogest/prawn-svg] v1.0.0
item.description:
mogest/prawn-svg | 200 stars| 65 forks.

| Ruby | Shell | CSS |

SVG renderer for Prawn Ruby PDF library

After around 16 years, prawn-svg covers enough of SVG 1.1 and is robust enough to call it 1.0.

This release turns web requests off by default, replaces warnings with categorised issues that can raise, puts a work limit on every render, and hardens prawn-svg against hostile SVGs.

Upgrading from 0.40

Web requests are off by default

As announced in 0.40, prawn-svg no longer fetches http: or https: URLs unless you ask it to. If you didn't set :enable_web_requests, remote images, fonts, stylesheets and <use> references are now skipped and reported as :resource issues.

web_requests: true sends requests through ssrf_filter, which refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses. For trusted SVGs that need internal hosts, pass web_requests: Prawn::SVG::Requests::Unfiltered.new. :web_requests also takes your own callable if you want to completely control how requests are made; see Web requests.

Responses are capped at 20 MB and 30 seconds per request. Content fetched from the web can now only refer to other web or data: URLs, so it can't read local files.

Renamed options

The old names are still accepted; if both are given, the new one wins.

0.40 1.0
enable_web_requests: true web_requests: true
enable_file_requests_with_root: path file_requests: path
cache_images: true the default; see below
cache_images: false cache_requests: false
log_warnings: true log_issues: true
result[:warnings] result[:issues], whose messages are the same strings
Prawn::SVG::Document::InvalidSVGData Prawn::SVG::InvalidSVGData
Prawn::SVG::Document::Error Prawn::SVG::Error

:file_requests also takes a callable, for example to serve files from memory. file_requests: "/" now works; previously it refused every path.

Every request is now cached for the length of a render. To share a cache between renders, pass your own Hash as :cache_requests.

Unknown options raise

Unknown options, including string keys such as "at", now raise ArgumentError. Previously they were ignored unless Prawn.debug was on.

Warnings are now issues

svg returns result[:issues], an array of Prawn::SVG::Issue objects with a category (:unsupported, :unknown, :invalid or :resource) and a message. prawn-svg now reports far more than it used to: unsupported elements, attributes and properties, unknown tags and attributes, values it can't use, references to missing elements, and resources it couldn't load. If you checked result[:warnings].empty?, filter result[:issues] by category instead.

raise_on_issue: raises Prawn::SVG::IssueError after rendering if any issue occurred. Give it a category or array of categories to raise only on those:

svg data, raise_on_issue: [:unsupported, :invalid, :resource]

Document#warnings now returns a frozen array.

Work limit

Each render now has a work budget, :max_work, defaulting to 1_000_000. One unit is roughly an element, a drawing call, a character of text or a few hundred bytes of image data, counted every time <use>, markers, patterns, masks and clip paths repeat them. If the budget is exceeded, Prawn::SVG::WorkLimitExceeded is raised before anything is drawn. result[:work] reports the work a render used.

Very large drawings can hit the default, such as a plot with tens of thousands of <use> markers or a path with millions of points. Raise :max_work, or pass false to turn the limit off for trusted input.

Elements nested more than 200 deep now make the SVG invalid, and XML entity expansion is capped at 10 MB.

Requirements

  • Prawn 2.3.0 or later (previously 0.11.1).
  • Ruby 2.7 or later, tested up to Ruby 4.0.
  • New runtime dependencies: ssrf_filter and addressable (2.9.1 or later).

Removed

  • Prawn::SVG::Interface.font_path. Use Prawn::SVG::FontRegistry.font_path.
  • UrlLoader#add_to_cache and UrlLoader#retrieve_from_cache. Pass a pre-filled Hash as :cache_requests.

Other behaviour changes

  • @font-face fonts no longer leak into the Prawn document's font_families after svg returns, or between SVGs nested in the same render.
  • @font-face fonts are checked by rendering the SVG's text with them; fonts that fail are reported as :resource issues and skipped.
  • Installed fonts that Prawn can't use are skipped instead of crashing.
  • Characters a built-in PDF font can't encode are replaced instead of raising.
  • SVGs loaded through <image> now inherit :color_mode, :fallback_font_name, :web_requests and the outer document's fonts, and report their issues in the outer result. They can't read local files.
  • Conditional processing attributes (requiredFeatures, requiredExtensions, systemLanguage) are evaluated on every element that supports them, not just inside <switch>.
  • An SVG with zero width or height is no longer reported; a negative size is reported as :invalid.
  • The gem now ships only lib, README.md and LICENSE.

Fixes

  • Exponents in lengths and percentages (1e2, 5E-1%).
  • Angle units (deg, rad, grad) in marker orient.
  • objectBoundingBox fractions given as lengths or percentages.
  • <tspan> inside <textPath>.
  • Soft masks nested inside soft masks.
  • <tref> renders only character data, resolves references to any element including later ones, and ignores missing references.
  • <text> properties are applied once.
  • TTF fonts use the font's own underline position.
  • Gradients referenced before their definition inherit the right properties; gradient <stop>s see their inherited properties.
  • Whitespace around text coordinate lists and textPath startOffset percentages is ignored.
  • A viewBox that isn't four numbers is ignored; zero-sized nested viewports are skipped.
  • Only usable width and height values are copied from <use> to <symbol>.
  • An invalid @import no longer discards the rest of its stylesheet.
  • UTF-16 and UTF-32 SVGs are parsed instead of crashing.
  • vposition error message lists :center, not :right.

Hardening

  • Malformed or degenerate input no longer hangs or crashes: path data not starting with a moveto, closepath followed by a number, empty paths with markers or textPath, degenerate gradients with spreadMethod, empty gradients, self-referencing <use>, masks, clip paths, gradients and patterns.
  • Non-finite numbers are kept out of the PDF.
  • Corrupt images (including truncated PNGs), fonts, stylesheets and XML entities are reported as issues rather than raising.
  • The file loader rejects directories, null bytes, opaque file: URLs and symlinks that leave the root.
  • CSS selectors are matched in linear time without XPath, and selector values can't inject XPath.
  • Long attribute values no longer trigger quadratic parsing.

Performance

  • The font registry is only loaded when an SVG has text, and is no longer rebuilt every render.
  • Images are decoded once, when drawn.
  • Element lookups by id, namespace resolution and tree walking no longer scale quadratically with document size.

item.description:
kivikakk/comrak | 1749 stars| 207 forks.

| Rust | Shell | Makefile | Nix | HTML | CSS | JavaScript |

CommonMark + GFM compatible Markdown parser and renderer

Remember this line from earlier this week?

  • Any option or extension currently without a complete write-up per #924 is liable to change output in the minor version it gets its spec! It'll probably be in very edge-case-y ways you might never have run into, but be warned.

WE'RE HERE. Enjoy!

Parser changes:

  • Footnotes have been specced, with some changes. (by @kivikakk in #935)
    • When a label is defined more than once, the first definition takes precedence, like cmark-gfm. Before, every definition was rendered!
    • Definitions nested inside other definitions are now found.
    • Labels match as written in the source: [^a] no longer matches [^a], and [^`b`] now matches [^`b`]:. Unmatched references are just left as-is: [^*b*] renders emphasis!
    • Footnotes are numbered in reading order; references inside definitions are numbered after the references thereto. Definitions only referenced from unreferenced definitions are dropped.
    • A blank line inside a container, or a line of only spaces, no longer end a footnote definition.
  • Wikilinks have been specced, likewise with some changes. (by @kivikakk in #936)
    • An unclosed [ no longer stops a following wikilink from parsing, meaning [blah [[Home]] now links [[Home]] like you'd expect.
    • A wikilink inside link text stops the outer link forming, as a link would, and wikilinks now parse in image descriptions.
    • Line endings in wikilink destinations become spaces, not %0A.
  • Alert marker are now much more like blockquotes wrt. spacing: >[!note] and up to three spaces or a tab after the > now start an alert, and for multiline alerts too. (by @kivikakk in #938)
  • Attributes have been specced, with (you guessed it!) some changes. (by @kivikakk in #939)
    • Keys may start with _ or :, values may be unquoted (e.g. {k=a/b}), and entities in values are decoded.
    • id= and class= pairs set the ID and add classes; the last ID or pair with a given key takes precedence; consecutive attribute blocks on inline code and links get merged, e.g. `x`{.a}{#b}.
    • Fenced code attributes are parsed from the info string as written, thus \{ and { no longer start them.

Changed APIs:

  • With render.attributes, Comrak's own HTML attributes now take precedence over parsed ones, instead of being overridden, and we don't emit any attribute twice. [a](/u){href=/v} gets href="/u". (by @kivikakk in #939)

Bug fixes:

  • NodeFootnoteReference::texts holds the label as written in the source, instead of one rebuilt from parsed inlines. So long, "awful HACK". (by @kivikakk in #935)
  • An empty footnote definition's <li> is followed by a newline in HTML. (by @kivikakk in #935)
  • Wikilinks roundtrip through the CommonMark formatter, no longer attracting a duplicate title or percent-encoded labels. (by @kivikakk in #936)
  • The CommonMark formatter percent-encodes control characters in link URLs correctly (%09, not % 9 D:). (by @kivikakk in #936)
  • The CommonMark formatter keeps the > on blank lines after code and HTML blocks in blockquotes. (by @kivikakk in #938)
  • The CommonMark formatter escapes alert titles! (by @kivikakk in #938)
  • The CommonMark formatter writes attributes, and escapes text that would otherwise parse as attributes. (by @kivikakk in #939)

Documentation:

  • Document footnotes, wikilinks, alerts, and attributes with care. (by @kivikakk in #935, #936, #938, #939)
  • comrak.ee differentias finished specs and drafts. (by @kivikakk in 140a1a1, #938, and #939)
  • The README links our GFM extension specs, and documents our stability guarantees. (931f5e4, 8129ed5, 448a093)
